correctness.rationale: Symmetric equilibrium follows from player indifference. The exact forward-difference factorization (7) and strict Karamata majorization (8)–(9) establish all threshold orderings and global maximizer cases. The packaged verifier passed 660 exact rational identity instances and 825 floating checks; finite experiments are not treated as proof for all n.

originality.rationale: The novelty is the full finite-size strict crossover ladder and exactly one-peaked classification, including every tie and the 4/3 near-critical drift, not the classical payoff game, mixed Nash probability, falling success probability or large-size limit. The main closest source analyzes group-size effects primarily for contributor thresholds above one, recording the canonical k=1 expected-count formula but not deriving the claimed all-size ordered crossings in inspected source text. Residual textbook-equivalence risk is material and stated.
residual_risks: The one-volunteer equilibrium is a textbook model and an equivalent finite-size sequence inequality may already have appeared in game-theory books, including Dixit et al. (2004), pp. 454–458, which were not fully inspected.
The primary 1985 journal full text was not accessible, so its finite-size comparisons were not exhaustively checked.
Searches cannot exclude a reparameterized inequality in economics or discrete convexity literature; no independent external audit has yet occurred.

value.rationale: The expected total number of contributors is the actual aggregate burden of paying individual volunteering costs when one volunteer suffices. Knowing its globally maximizing finite group size and how it diverges as c/b approaches e^-2 is a motivated comparative-statics question, distinct from decreasing success probability and from asymptotic monotonicity. The exact strict-majorization proof rules out multiple peaks, and the 4/3 coefficient quantifies the boundary layer. No claim is made for broader public-goods thresholds or policy outcomes.
